title: Existence of scattering limits for the defocusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation
statement:
For the defocusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation on $\mathbb{R}^d$ defined on page 45, with $d>1$, the report states that
\[
\lim_{t\to\pm\infty}\Phi^{-t}\varphi_t(u)=:u_\pm=\Omega_\pm(u)
\]
exists in $H^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$.
completeness_reason: Flow maps, page-45 equation, initial-data class and admissible dimension/regularity are not supplied.
quantifiers: For all intended u and d>1, both time-direction limits in H1.
technical_assessment: Duhamel scattering needs spacetime integrability and global well-posedness in the specified class; d>1 alone does not supply these. No full-dimensional route.

title: Existence of a small even large-image Galois representation
statement: Does there exist a prime $p<1{,}000{,}000$ and an even representation $\rho:G_{\mathbb Q}\to\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb F_p)$, unramified outside $p$, whose image contains $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb F_p)$?
completeness_reason: Existential prime bound, parity, ramification and image conditions are specified using standard representation terminology.
quantifiers: Exists prime p<1000000 and even continuous Galois representation unramified outside p with SL2 image containment.
technical_assessment: A number-field certificate would need ramification, Galois group and complex-conjugation verification; enumerating primes is not an enumeration of such extensions.

title: Rational points on non-split Cartan modular curves
statement:
Does there exist a constant $c$ such that, for every prime number $p>c$, the only $
Q$-points of the modular curve $X_{\mathrm{ns}}(p)$ over $
Q$ are CM points? Here $X_{\mathrm{ns}}(n)$ is the quotient of the full-level modular curve $X(n)$ by the normalizer $C_{\mathrm{ns}}^{+}(n)$ of a non-split Cartan subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})$.
completeness_reason: The quotient curve and eventual prime quantifiers are supplied; malformed Q markup is readable.
quantifiers: Exists c for every prime p>c all rational points of the normalizer quotient are CM.
technical_assessment: A finite rational-point computation cannot establish the uniform prime cutoff; needs global uniformity, not a fixed-p certificate.

title: Algorithm for enumerating relative cubic extensions over imaginary quadratic fields
statement:
Let $K$ be an imaginary quadratic number field with class number $h_K=1$. For $X>0$, let
\[
\mathcal F_{K,3}(X)=\{\text{isomorphism classes of extensions }L/K:[L:K]=3,\ \mathcal N_{K/\mathbb Q}(\mathfrak d(L/K))\le X\}.
\]
There exists an algorithm that lists all cubic extensions in $\mathcal F_{K,3}(X)$ in time $O_{\varepsilon}(X^{1+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$.
completeness_reason: Runtime model, output representation and dependence on K are unspecified.
quantifiers: For class-number-one imaginary quadratic K and all X>0 enumerate every relative cubic field within X in O_epsilon(X^(1+epsilon)).
technical_assessment: Binary cubic forms and reduction are plausible established mechanisms; complexity and completeness require exact reduction/domain conventions and a theorem-body comparison.

title: Maximal Riesz-transform boundedness versus variational boundedness
statement: Given an arbitrary nonatomic measure \(\mu\) on \(\mathbb{R}^d\), does boundedness of the maximal Riesz transform \(R_*^\mu\) on \(L^2(\mu)\) imply boundedness of \(\mathcal{V}_\rho\circ R^\mu\) on \(L^2(\mu)\), for \(\rho>2\)?
completeness_reason: Dimension/order of the Riesz kernel and truncation/variation definitions for arbitrary nonatomic measures are omitted.
quantifiers: For every intended nonatomic mu and rho>2, maximal L2 boundedness implies variational L2 boundedness.
technical_assessment: Maximal control does not itself bound accumulated oscillation; a jump/variation estimate is the missing mechanism.

title: Semiregular automorphisms of finite vertex-transitive graphs
statement: Does every finite vertex-transitive graph have a semiregular automorphism, that is, an automorphism whose cycles all have the same length $\ll>1$?
completeness_reason: No nontrivial-order restriction is given on finite vertex-transitive graphs.
quantifiers: Every finite vertex-transitive graph has a nonidentity automorphism all of whose cycles have equal length.
technical_assessment: The one-vertex graph has only identity. This endpoint observation earns no credit; the substantive nontrivial polycirculant problem needs structural group theory.

title: Existence of an extremal binary code of length 72
statement: Does there exist an extremal doubly-even self-dual binary code of length $72$?
completeness_reason: Standard extremal doubly-even self-dual binary code terminology determines the finite existence target.
quantifiers: Exists binary self-dual doubly-even length72 code attaining extremal minimum distance16.
technical_assessment: A 36x72 generator could certify existence with exact weight verification, but no construction or bounded exhaustive classification is available here.

title: Higman’s PORC conjecture
statement: For each fixed $n$, let $f_n(p)$ denote the number of groups of order $p^n$, where $p$ ranges over the primes. Higman’s conjecture is that $f_n(p)$ is polynomial on residue classes (PORC): there exist polynomials $g_1(p),\ldots,g_k(p)$ and a positive integer $N$ such that, for every prime $p$, $f_n(p)=g_i(p)$ for some $i$, with the choice of $i$ depending only on the residue class of $p\pmod N$.
completeness_reason: PORC definition and prime/uniform fixed-n scope are explicit.
quantifiers: For every fixed positive n exists modulus and finitely many polynomial residue formulas for counts of order p^n groups.
technical_assessment: Special n counts cannot establish all n; a general classification/counting mechanism is absent.

title: PORC behavior of the number of groups of order $p^{10}$
statement: Is the total number of groups of order $p^{10}$, as a function of the prime $p$, a PORC function?
completeness_reason: PORC is not defined in this literal, though the neighboring assigned record supplies its standard interpretation.
quantifiers: As prime p varies, total order-p^10 group count is PORC.
technical_assessment: Requires full isomorphism counting across all primes; a few prime computations or a non-PORC subfamily do not determine the total.

title: Gal’s conjecture for flag simple polytopes
statement: **Conjecture 1 (Gal, 2005).** Any flag simple $n$-polytope $P$ satisfies $\\gamma_i(P^n) \\ge 0$ for $i=0,\\ldots,\\left\\lfloor n/2\\right\\rfloor$.
completeness_reason: The gamma vector normalization is not defined in the literal.
quantifiers: Every flag simple n-polytope has nonnegative gamma_i for 0<=i<=floor(n/2).
technical_assessment: Face-number reformulation does not furnish a uniform positivity mechanism; low-dimensional instances are insufficient.

title: Strong universal consistency in static forecasting under mere integrability
statement:
Does there exist a sequence of static forecasting estimates $m_n(X_0,D_{-1}^{-n})$ such that, for every stationary and ergodic sequence $((X_n,Y_n))_{n\in\mathbb Z}$ of $\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R$-valued random variables satisfying $\mathbb E|Y_0|<\infty$, one has
\[
m_n(X_0,D_{-1}^{-n})\longrightarrow \mathbb E\!\left[Y_0\mid X_{-\infty}^{0},Y_{-\infty}^{-1}\right]\quad\text{almost surely}?
\]
completeness_reason: The observed data D and admissible static estimate/measurability conventions are not defined.
quantifiers: Exists one estimator sequence valid almost surely for every stationary ergodic integrable real-response process.
technical_assessment: Truncating bounded-response estimators requires uniform almost-sure control over truncation and ergodic rates; integrability alone does not justify exchanging limits.

title: Theta-function norm bounds for general groups and lattices
statement: For what groups $G$ and lattices $\Gamma$ can one prove such bounds for all theta functions?
completeness_reason: Such bounds and theta-function class are absent.
quantifiers: Classify G,Gamma satisfying an unspecified bound for all unspecified theta functions.
technical_assessment: No inequality, norm, normalization or parameter range is present; no substitute question adopted.

title: Sup-norm bound for Hecke–Maass newforms of square-free level
statement:
Let $f$ be an $L^2$-normalized Hecke–Maass cuspidal newform of square-free level $N$, with trivial nebentypus and Laplacian eigenvalue $\$. Prove that, for every $\>0$,

$$\ f\_\\infty\ \ll_{\,\u001b} N^{-1/6+\},$$

where the implied constant depends continuously on $\$.
completeness_reason: Control characters and missing eigenvalue, epsilon and norm symbols corrupt the asserted bound.
quantifiers: Intended all square-free N sup-norm exponent -1/6+epsilon, with unreadable dependencies.
technical_assessment: Cannot certify a literal analytic inequality with missing variables; a reconstructed familiar bound would not be this record.

title: Lindelöf hypothesis for the Riemann zeta-function
statement: For every \4\varepsilon>0\4, \(\zeta(\tfrac12+it)\ll t^{\varepsilon}\) as \(t\to\infty\).
completeness_reason: Despite extraneous control markup, the epsilon and large-t inequality are identifiable.
quantifiers: For every epsilon>0 zeta(1/2+it)=O_epsilon(t^epsilon) as t tends to positive infinity.
technical_assessment: No subpolynomial critical-line bound follows from finite values or fixed-exponent estimates; no short full-scope route.

title: Purdy’s conjecture on planes versus lines determined by points in 3-space
statement: For all sufficiently large $n$, let $P$ be a set of $n$ points in $3$-space such that the points do not all lie on two skew lines and no plane contains $n-1$ of the points. If $p$ is the number of planes determined by $P$ and $l$ is the number of lines determined by $P$, then $p\ge l$.
completeness_reason: Geometric exclusions and sufficiently-large-n quantifier are explicit.
quantifiers: For all sufficiently large finite real 3-space configurations outside two listed degeneracies, determined planes>=lines.
technical_assessment: Counting point-plane incidences must handle arbitrary collinear/coplanar concentrations; small configurations cannot settle eventual scope.

title: Algorithmic undecidability of topological $d$-representability
statement: For every fixed integer $d\ge 5$, it is algorithmically undecidable, given a finite simplicial complex $K$ abstractly as a collection of faces, whether $K$ is topologically $d$-representable; that is, whether $K$ is isomorphic to the nerve of a finite good cover of open sets in $\mathbb{R}^d$, where every nonempty subcollection has intersection either empty or contractible.
completeness_reason: Nerve, good-cover class, input format and dimension quantifiers are explicitly defined.
quantifiers: For every fixed d>=5 recognition of finite nerves of good covers in R^d is undecidable.
technical_assessment: Primary report Theorem1 p2481 explicitly states this exact result and p2482 gives a Novikov-based reduction sketch; no new outcome, no full proof-dependency audit claimed.

title: Circle-freeness of Minkowski sums with a ball
statement: Is it true that for every circle-free convex body $K$, the set $K+B$ is also circle-free?
completeness_reason: Circle-free and B are not defined in the literal; source supplies holding by circles in R3 and a ball.
quantifiers: For every circle-free convex body K, K+B remains circle-free.
technical_assessment: Primary p2498 defines the condition and proves only planar X plus ball; that special case does not subsume arbitrary K. No full-scope motion obstruction constructed.

title: Crossing-number lower bound for arbitrary drawings of complete graphs
statement:
For every integer $n\ge 4$, does every drawing of the complete graph $K_n$ have at least
$$\frac14\left\lfloor\frac n2\right\rfloor\left\lfloor\frac{n-1}2\right\rfloor\left\lfloor\frac{n-2}2\right\rfloor\left\lfloor\frac{n-3}2\right\rfloor$$
crossings?
completeness_reason: Arbitrary drawing lacks conventions on edge intersections, tangencies and multiplicity.
quantifiers: For every n>=4 every admissible drawing of K_n has at least the displayed four-floor product divided by4 crossings.
technical_assessment: Literal degeneracies cannot earn credit; under standard proper-drawing conventions this is a uniform crossing-number target, not settled by checking small n.

title: Anchored rectangle packing conjecture
statement: For every finite point set $S\subseteq U=[0,1]^2$ with $(0,0)\in S$, where Bob must choose for each $s\in S$ an axis-parallel rectangle $r(s)\subseteq U$ having $s$ as its lower-left corner, with the rectangle interiors pairwise disjoint and with no point of $S$ in the interior of any $r(s)$, can Bob always choose the rectangles so that their total area is at least $\frac12$?
completeness_reason: Anchors, square, forbidden points, disjoint interiors and area threshold are given.
quantifiers: Every finite S in unit square containing origin admits the specified packing with area>=1/2.
technical_assessment: Greedy local rectangles can block later anchors; need a uniform charging/decomposition argument, not a single arrangement certificate.

title: Integral lattices and embeddings into integer lattices
statement: A lattice $L$ in a Euclidean space is called an integral lattice if the inner product $\langle x,y\rangle$ is an integer for every $x,y\in L$. Is every integral lattice $L$ congruent to a sub-lattice of $\mathbb{Z}^n$ for some $n$?
completeness_reason: Integrality, congruence and existential ambient dimension are explicit.
quantifiers: Every integral Euclidean lattice is isometric to a sublattice of Z^n for some n.
technical_assessment: Even unimodular E8 gives a classical obstruction; exact Gram/inverse certificate executed here. Primary p2538 states the literal question. No novelty or registry clearance; no proposal for this standard-lattice adaptation.

title: Bounded monotone paths in convex plane subdivisions with three unbounded rays
statement: Is there a constant $c$ such that, for every $n\ge 3$, there is a partition of the plane into convex regions whose boundaries form a connected graph with $n$ vertices and $3$ unbounded rays, such that every monotone path in the graph consists of at most $c$ edges? Here a path is monotone if there is some linear function $\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}$ that is strictly monotone along the path.
completeness_reason: Uniform edge bound, all n, ray count, convexity and monotonicity are defined.
quantifiers: Exists constant c for every n>=3 some convex subdivision with n graph vertices and three unbounded rays has all monotone paths length<=c.
technical_assessment: A construction must simultaneously block every linear direction while retaining convex faces; no scalable local gadget established.

title: Doubly covered paths for coverings by unit discs
statement: Is there a constant $c$ such that, for every covering of the plane by closed unit circular discs, any two points situated at distance $d$ from one another and covered by at least two discs can be connected by a path of length at most $\\sqrt{2}d+c$ traveling within the part of the plane covered by at least two discs?
completeness_reason: All unit-disc coverings, doubly covered endpoints, universal additive c and length bound are explicit.
quantifiers: Exists c independent of covering and endpoints, doubly covered path length<=sqrt(2)d+c.
technical_assessment: Even connectivity of the doubly covered region needs geometric control; a finite sampled covering is not the all-coverings assertion.

title: Algebraic K-theory Novikov conjecture for group algebras over Schatten class operators
statement: For the ring of Schatten class operators and every group $G$, the associated algebraic $K$-theory assembly map is rationally injective. Consequently, the algebraic $K$-theory Novikov conjecture holds for all group algebras over the ring of Schatten class operators.
completeness_reason: Assembly-map domain and family conventions are omitted.
quantifiers: For every group G the Schatten-coefficient K-theory assembly is rationally injective.
technical_assessment: Literal is an affirmative report, not evidence of novelty; operator-ideal and controlled-algebra dependencies preclude a small certificate route here.

title: Numerical characterization of Du Bois singularities
statement: Let $X$ be a proper variety over $\mathbb{C}$ with a fixed basepoint-free linear system $\Delta$. Then $X$ has only Du Bois singularities if and only if $h^i(L,\mathcal{O}_L)\leq f_{0,i}(L)$ for $i>0$ and for every $L\subseteq X$ that is the intersection of general members of $\Delta$.
completeness_reason: The Hodge-theoretic quantity f_0,i is not defined.
quantifiers: Every proper complex variety with basepoint-free Delta is Du Bois iff the numerical inequalities hold on every general complete intersection in positive degree.
technical_assessment: The equivalence requires the exact Hodge filtration comparison and hyperplane-induction hypotheses; simple Euler characteristics do not settle it.

title: Conservativity of weak intuitionistic constructive set theories over arithmetic
statement: For every weak set theory $T$ in question and every arithmetical statement $A$, $T \vdash A \Longleftrightarrow HA + TI(<\lvert T\rvert) \vdash A$, where $TI(<\lvert T\rvert)$ denotes the arithmetical transfinite-induction scheme below the proof-theoretic ordinal of $T$.
completeness_reason: Weak theories T in question and their ordinal notations are not specified.
quantifiers: For each unspecified T and every arithmetic A, equivalence with HA plus transfinite induction below ordinal(T).
technical_assessment: Cannot fix a conservation endpoint without the axioms and ordinal presentation; no proof-theoretic substitute chosen.

title: Universality and polynomial-time solvability of fixed-parameter three-dimensional table integer programs
statement:
Consider the integer optimization problem
\[
\min\left\{wx:\ x\in\mathbb Z_{+}^{3\times m\times n},\ \sum_i x_{i,j,k}=a_{j,k},\ \sum_j x_{i,j,k}=b_{i,k},\ \sum_k x_{i,j,k}=c_{i,j}\right\}.
\]
Every integer program can be put precisely into this form; and, for any fixed parameter \(m\), this problem can be solved in polynomial time with variable \(n\).
completeness_reason: Precisely into this form omits reduction/encoding, and runtime dependence on fixed m is implicit.
quantifiers: Every integer program reduces to the displayed 3xm xn table form; for each fixed m solve in polynomial time over variable n.
technical_assessment: Universality and n-fold integer programming are distinct obligations; established machinery may prove both but a bare assertion cannot establish new eligibility.

title: Boyd–Carr conjecture on the 2-matching/subtour-LP ratio
statement: For symmetric traveling-salesman instances whose costs satisfy the triangle inequality, the worst-case ratio of the cost of an optimal 2-matching to the cost of an optimal solution of the subtour linear program is at most $10/9$. Here a 2-matching is an integer solution satisfying the subtour-LP degree and bound constraints, without the subtour-elimination constraints.
completeness_reason: Metric costs, degree/bound-only integer solutions and subtour LP comparison are specified.
quantifiers: For every symmetric metric TSP instance optimal 2-matching<=10/9 times subtour LP optimum.
technical_assessment: Need global rounding preserving costs at exact factor; fractional extreme-point examples cannot prove the upper bound.

title: Residual-chain approximation for normalized first Betti numbers
statement:
For which groups $G$ does the limit
\[
\lim_{i\in I}\frac{b_1(G_i;K)}{[G:G_i]}
\]
exist for all systems $(G_i)_{i\in I}$ with $\bigcap_{i\in I}G_i=\{1\}$ and fields $K$, and is independent of the choice of $(G_i)_{i\in I}$ and $K$?
completeness_reason: Systems G_i lack normality, finite-index and directedness conditions in the literal.
quantifiers: Classify groups with field- and system-independent normalized b1 limits for every trivial-intersection system.
technical_assessment: Different system classes change the problem; do not silently replace this row with the more precise next record.

title: Normalized first Betti numbers in finite-index subgroup systems
statement:
For which groups $G$ does the limit
$$
\lim_{i\in I}\frac{b_1(G_i;K)}{[G:G_i]}
$$
exist for every inverse system $(G_i)_{i\in I}$ of normal finite-index subgroups of $G$, directed by inclusion, satisfying $\bigcap_{i\in I}G_i=\{1\}$, and for every field $K$, with the resulting limit independent of both the system $(G_i)_{i\in I}$ and the field $K$?
completeness_reason: Normal finite-index inverse systems, trivial intersection and fields are specified.
quantifiers: Classify G for which every such residual system and every K gives the same normalized b1 limit.
technical_assessment: Characteristic-zero approximation does not automatically give field independence; a classification needs control of mod-p homology gradients.

title: Uniqueness of 7-dimensional regular Riemannian foliations of spheres
statement: The report conjectured that there are no 7-dimensional regular Riemannian foliations of spheres other than the Hopf fibration $S^7 \to S^{15} \to S^8$.
completeness_reason: Sphere metric, equivalence of foliations and possible zero-dimensional/trivial cases are not fixed.
quantifiers: Every 7-dimensional regular Riemannian sphere foliation is the S15 Hopf fibration in the intended sense.
technical_assessment: Riemannian-submersion classification needs geometric hypotheses and equivalence convention; no short independent route.

title: K-triviality and weak ML-cuppability
statement: For every set $A$, $A$ is weakly ML-cuppable if and only if $A$ is not $K$-trivial, where $A$ is weakly ML-cuppable if there is an incomplete Martin-Löf random set $X$ such that $A\oplus X\geq_T\emptyset'.$
completeness_reason: For every set A lacks the usual computability/domain restriction on A if any; K-triviality is not defined.
quantifiers: A is weakly ML-cuppable iff A is not K-trivial, using incomplete ML-random X cupping to the jump.
technical_assessment: Quantifying over arbitrary A rather than a source-specified complexity class can alter the equivalence; needs exact primary scope and known cupping theorem comparison.

title: Uniform computation of maximal chains in computable well partial orders
statement: There is no hyperarithmetic procedure $f$ such that, for every index $e$ for a computable well partial order $P$, the function $n\mapsto f(e,n)$ is the characteristic function of a maximal chain of $P$. In fact, every such procedure $f$ computes every hyperarithmetic set.
completeness_reason: Maximal chain may mean inclusion-maximal or maximal order type; procedure representation is unstated.
quantifiers: Every uniform chain selector for all computable wpo indices computes every hyperarithmetic set; none is hyperarithmetic.
technical_assessment: Inclusion-maximal versus maximum-order-type chains have very different selector complexity; no interpretation chosen silently.

title: Uniqueness of identifying a mixed-boundary obstacle and its impedance from full far-field data
statement:
For the two-dimensional exterior Helmholtz problem described in (1), with 
\(\partial D=\partial D_D\cup\partial D_I\), the boundary components \(\partial D_D\), \(\partial D_I\), and the impedance \(\lambda(x)\) on \(\partial D_I\) are uniquely determined by the far-field data \(u^\infty(\hat x)\) for all measurement points \(\hat x\) and all incident directions \(d\).
completeness_reason: Equation(1), obstacle regularity, impedance class and frequency conditions are missing.
quantifiers: All observation and incident directions uniquely determine mixed boundary components and impedance for the intended exterior Helmholtz problem.
technical_assessment: Rellich plus continuation is a possible classical route only after the boundary and impedance assumptions are specified.

title: Convergence analysis for the regularized inverse-scattering iteration
statement: It is an open problem to extend the convergence analysis to the modification of iteration (10) in which $S$ is replaced by $S_n:=N_{\rho,\alpha_n}\circ R$, where $N_{\rho,\alpha_n}$ is a Tikhonov regularization of the Cauchy operator $N_\rho$ with a null sequence of regularization parameters $\alpha_n$.
completeness_reason: Iteration(10), spaces, R, convergence notion and parameter schedule conditions are absent.
quantifiers: Extend convergence analysis to an unspecified iteration with Tikhonov-regularized Cauchy operator and alpha_n tending to zero.
technical_assessment: Noise amplification and parameter coupling cannot be bounded without the actual recurrence and assumptions.

title: Macdonald polynomials at $t=0$ and normalized $q$-Whittaker functions
statement: Conjecture 0.9 asserts that, for every weight $\check\lambda$ under consideration, $$P_{\check\lambda}(q,0,z)=\widehat\Psi_{\check\lambda}(q,z).$$
completeness_reason: Weights under consideration and normalized q-Whittaker functions are undefined.
quantifiers: For every intended coweight P_lambda(q,0,z)=normalized Psi_lambda(q,z).
technical_assessment: Eigenfunction uniqueness may prove identity only with normalization and parameter domains fixed; no full route certified.

title: Origin of the characteristic length of persistent shear bands
statement: For granular materials undergoing shear, what determines the characteristic rolling-correlation length associated with persistent shear bands, whose typical width is about 10–20 particle diameters?
completeness_reason: An empirical explanatory question supplies no mathematical model or quantified endpoint.
quantifiers: Determine characteristic rolling-correlation scale for shear bands around10-20 particle diameters.
technical_assessment: A model-dependent mechanism cannot constitute a theorem answering the literal without constitutive equations and observable definitions.

title: Conjugacy of maximal invariant 2-subgroups in {2,3}-groups
statement: Let $G$ be a ${2,3}$-group whose Sylow $3$-subgroups have exponent $3$. Then, for every element $x\in G$ of order $3$, all maximal $x$-invariant $2$-subgroups of $G$ are conjugate via $C_G(x)$.
completeness_reason: Whether {2,3}-group is finite or periodic/local is unspecified.
quantifiers: For each such G with exponent3 Sylow3 groups and each order3 x, maximal x-invariant2 subgroups form one C_G(x)-orbit.
technical_assessment: Finite coprime action may help, but does not extend automatically to unspecified infinite periodic groups; no full-scope conjugacy mechanism.

title: Verification of the inductive conditions for all simple groups and primes
statement: Do the inductive McKay and inductive blockwise Alperin weight conditions hold for every simple group and every prime?
completeness_reason: The inductive McKay and blockwise Alperin weight conditions are not stated.
quantifiers: For every simple group and prime both inductive conditions hold.
technical_assessment: Verification requires full finite-simple-group/character-theory families and exceptional cases; no bounded small certificate route.

title: Non-commutative Waring problem for finite non-abelian simple groups
statement: Let $w\in F_d$ be a non-trivial word in the free group on $d$ generators. Then there exists a constant $N=N(w)$ depending on $w$ such that, for every finite non-abelian simple group $G$ with $|G|>N$, one has $w(G)^2=G$.
completeness_reason: Word, threshold dependence, simplicity and double image product are explicit.
quantifiers: For every nontrivial free word w exists N(w), all finite nonabelian simple G larger than N satisfy w(G)^2=G.
technical_assessment: A familiar Waring-type theorem endpoint; needs actual primary/successor body before any investment. No threshold mechanism developed and no novelty claim.

title: Products of two squares in finite quasisimple groups
statement: Every element in any finite quasisimple group $G$ is a product of two squares; equivalently, for every $g\in G$, there exist $x,y\in G$ such that $g=x^2y^2$.
completeness_reason: Standard finite quasisimplicity and elementwise factorization are explicit.
quantifiers: For every finite quasisimple G and every g exists x,y with g=x^2 y^2.
technical_assessment: Squares and real/character obstructions require all covers including exceptions; small-group checking would not prove the full theorem. Likely reported result, not cleared as novel.

title: E10 conjecture for eleven-dimensional supergravity
statement: The **E10 conjecture** asserts that the values of all fields of 11-dimensional supergravity and their spatial gradients can be mapped to a null geodesic motion in the infinite-dimensional coset space $E_{10}/K(E_{10})$.
completeness_reason: Map, fields, gradient completion, coset geometry and equivalence sense are unspecified.
quantifiers: All eleven-dimensional supergravity fields and spatial gradients admit the stated E10 null-geodesic mapping.
technical_assessment: Finite level truncations do not produce a full infinite-dimensional correspondence; formal dependencies are large.

title: Boundedness of continuous cohomology classes for simple Lie groups
statement:
For every connected simple Lie group $G$ with finite centre, is the natural comparison map
\[
H^\bullet_{\mathrm{cb}}(G;\mathbb{R})\longrightarrow H^\bullet_{\mathrm{c}}(G;\mathbb{R})
\]
surjective? Equivalently, is every class in $H^\bullet_{\mathrm{c}}(G;\mathbb{R})$ represented by a bounded continuous cocycle?
completeness_reason: Group class, coefficients and comparison-map surjectivity are explicit.
quantifiers: For every connected simple real Lie group with finite centre, every continuous-cohomology class has bounded continuous representative.
technical_assessment: Degree-two or Hermitian cases do not establish all degrees and real forms; no general bounded representative construction.

title: Rainbow matching conjecture
statement: Let $F_1,\\ldots,F_t$ be families of subsets in $\\binom{[n]}{k}$. If $|F_i|>\\max\\left\\{\\binom{n}{k}-\\binom{n-t+1}{k},\\binom{kt-1}{k}\\right\\}$ for every $1\\le i\\le t$, then there is a rainbow matching of size $t$: one that contains exactly one edge from each family.
completeness_reason: Families, common k-uniform ground set, strict threshold and rainbow size are explicit.
quantifiers: For all meaningful positive n,k,t, every t families exceeding the stated maximum admit disjoint representatives.
technical_assessment: Needs simultaneous transversal matching at sharp extremal thresholds; one-family extremal bounds do not imply rainbow selection.

title: Elashvili’s index conjecture for coadjoint stabilizers
statement: For every $p\in\mathfrak g^*$, $\operatorname{ind}\mathfrak g_p=\operatorname{ind}\mathfrak g$; here $\mathfrak g_p$ denotes the stabilizer of $p$ for the coadjoint action.
completeness_reason: The ambient Lie algebra g, base field and reductivity assumptions are absent.
quantifiers: For every p in an unspecified g dual, index of stabilizer equals index of g.
technical_assessment: The semisimple characteristic-zero theorem cannot be promoted as a result for unspecified Lie algebras; exact primary scope is necessary.

title: Higher-quiver cellular resolution conjecture for consistent toric algebras
statement: Conjecture: The statement of Theorem 0.2 holds for every consistent toric algebra of global dimension equal to $n=\dim X$. Namely, the higher quiver $\Delta\subset (S^1)^n$ exists, and the minimal projective $(A,A)$-bimodule resolution of $A$ is the cellular resolution determined by $\Delta$ as in Theorem 0.1.
completeness_reason: Theorem0.1/0.2 constructions and consistency conditions are absent.
quantifiers: All consistent toric algebras of global dimension n have a higher-quiver cellular bimodule resolution of the referenced kind.
technical_assessment: No cellular chain maps, incidence conventions or consistency axioms are supplied; no small resolution instance answers every algebra.

title: Classification of toric degenerations of low-degree smooth Fano threefolds
statement: All degenerations of smooth Fano threefolds of degree $\leq 12$ in their anticanonical embeddings to Gorenstein toric Fano varieties are completely classified.

title: Mahler’s conjecture on metric approximation by integer polynomials
statement:
For every fixed $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, for almost all real numbers $x$ there are only finitely many polynomials $P\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$ with $\deg P\le n$ such that
\[
|P(x)|<H(P)^{-n-\varepsilon},
\]
where $H(P)=\max_{0\le i\le n}|a_i|$ for $P(x)=\sum_{i=0}^{n}a_i x^i$.
completeness_reason: Degree, height and metric almost-everywhere finiteness quantifiers are explicit with standard positive-height convention.
quantifiers: For each n and epsilon>0 almost all real x admit only finitely many integral degree<=n P with abs(P(x))<H(P)^(-n-epsilon).
technical_assessment: Classical Mahler metric approximation endpoint; linear-polynomial Borel-Cantelli alone does not handle all degrees. No new credit or proof-body clearance claimed.

title: Yamabe invariant of cyclic quotients of the 5-sphere
statement:
It is conjectured that, for $M=S^5/(\cmathbb{Z}/m)$ with $m\ge 5$, the supremum in the definition of the smooth Yamabe invariant $\sigma(M)$ is attained by the round metric. This would imply
$$
\sigma(M)=\frac{\sigma(S^5)}{m^{2/5}}\approx\frac{78.996}{m^{2/5}}.
$$
completeness_reason: Cyclic action on S5 and normalization/admissibility of the round quotient are unspecified.
quantifiers: For each intended S5/(Z/m), m>=5, Yamabe invariant is round value sigma(S5)/m^(2/5).
technical_assessment: Finite-cover inequalities give bounds rather than the required supremum over conformal classes; distinct free actions must be fixed.

title: Compactness of the boundary Yamabe problem in dimensions n ≥ 25
statement: In analogy with the case without boundary, one wonders whether Theorem 1 is false when $n \ge 25$; namely, whether the stated compactness conclusion for the boundary Yamabe problem can fail in those dimensions.
completeness_reason: Theorem1 compactness hypotheses and boundary normalization are not included.

technical_assessment: Blow-up constructions depend on the missing geometric hypotheses; no dimension-threshold counterexample asserted.
